name: MOSS Voice
description: Your bots' voices: it speaks their replies aloud in each bot's voice, one at a time on this computer, through the voice provider the bot uses (Fish Audio, or another you add), and hears what you say with push-to-talk. Turned off, bots are text-only.

moss.voice.providers.doc: A voice provider: `speak` answers `{ text, voice, model?, format }` with the audio as it is made (pcm16-24k bytes, through points.stream); the optional `listen` answers `{ audio, format, model? }` (pcm16-16k bytes) with `{ text }`; the optional `ready` answers `{ ready, why? }`, whether the user set it up (its key or sign-in). A bot's voice names the entry's id.
moss.voice.providers.title: Voice providers

fills.ok: when you or a bot's default picks one of its voices, it is sent what your bots say, to speak it, and what you say with push-to-talk; what it writes down is sent to your bot as your message, with nothing shown to you first

moss.voice.modes.doc: The voice your bots speak and listen with, one at a time: the user's pick in Settings (the platform's picker, titled Voice), else MOSS Voice, which fills it itself. Another plugin's entry, while it is the one: `reply` is handed `{ bot, session, text, asked }` and speaks it its own way (its own background part, taking device/speech); `hear` is handed `{ bot, audio, format }` (what the user said with push-to-talk, pcm16-16k bytes) and answers `{ text }`.
moss.voice.modes.title: Voice

fills.ok: when you choose it, it is given what your bots say, to speak, and what you say with push-to-talk; what it writes down is sent to your bot as your message, with nothing shown to you first

moss.voice.defaults.doc: The default voice a plugin gives the bot it brings (the bot of its own tree; any other bot's is ignored): `provider` (an entry of moss.voice.providers) and `plugin` (the plugin that fills it, when another plugin's entry has the same id), `voice`, `model?`. The user's own choice in the bot's Voice section always wins, and a default speaks only when its provider says it is set up (its `ready`).
moss.voice.defaults.title: Default voices

fills.ok: sets the voice its bot speaks with; if you have set up that voice's provider, its bot's replies are sent to that provider on your account, and what it writes down from your push-to-talk is sent to your bot as your message, with nothing shown to you first

moss.voice.speech.doc: What MOSS Voice is saying and when, for a part that moves a mouth by it: MOSS Voice sends each plugin with an entry here, as point messages (`points.onMessage("moss.voice.speech")`), `{ bot, frames: [{ t, rms, centroid? }], cut? }`: mouth levels stamped in epoch milliseconds, loudness 0 to 1 and brightness in Hz, in batches a little ahead of when they sound, and `cut` when what was not yet sounded was stopped or replaced. Never the words, never the sound.
moss.voice.speech.title: Speech

fills.ok: it is told when your bots speak aloud, which bot and how loud, moment by moment, never their words

speakReplies.title: Speak replies
speakReplies.description: Your bots say their replies aloud with their voices. Off, they stay text-only.

provider.title: Voice provider
provider.description: The provider of this bot's voice (an entry of MOSS Voice's providers, such as fish-audio). Empty: the bot is text-only.

providerPlugin.title: Voice provider's plugin
providerPlugin.description: The plugin whose provider entry this bot's voice uses (when two plugins name an entry alike). Empty: the one plugin with that entry.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: This bot's voice, as its provider names it.

model.title: Voice model
model.description: The provider's voice model for this bot; empty is the provider's default.

silent.title: No voice
silent.description: This bot stays text-only: none of its replies are spoken, whatever its voice or its default.

commands.name: push-to-talk
commands.description: Hold Ctrl+Shift+Space to talk to the bot, as when you hold the talk button; let go to send.
